_by: Agent pass, 2026-10-18 (Claude). Each of the 31 needs-attention puzzles has one cause, from its milestone outputs (the text step's verdict and requests, assembly's checks, the manifest's answer grids); scans looked at for 6 of 81 puzzles to confirm a cause (7%). No puzzle content was typed.

causes.title: Looks ready: checked by the agent
causes.found: Read all 3 xd files against the text step's changes: all look right. 1978-09 L034's 'Ma that maas' (EWE) differs from gxd's 'Ma that baas', but it is printed that way (checked by Alex on the scan, 2026-10-18): kept as printed. A gxd one-letter near miss is not evidence of a misread; most of the 45 are style.

causes.title: Doubts the text step couldn't check
causes.stage: clue reading, and the text step's sheets
causes.found: Each puzzle's doubts are the orange marks on its proof page (about 3 per puzzle). In a sample of 6 marks on 3 puzzles, 3 were real losses the text step couldn't fix without a crop ('—— Karenina' read as '——'; a clue's second line dropped), and 3 were the right call. A loss shows at its mark, so checking the marks is enough.
causes.recommend: Walk the group on the proof page and look only at the orange marks: Ready if they look right, Not ready if one shows a loss (held for the clue-reading fix, which then re-runs only those). No line-by-line review.

causes.title: Key letters misread on the answer page
causes.found: Letters on a key's edge row (usually the last) lose their stems: OpenCV's opening counted past the image edge as ink (LANED read LAIFD). Traced by the key-reading session (branch claude/key-last-row); my first guess, keys printed touching, was wrong. The text step names the right answers in its verdict.
causes.recommend: Not ready yet. The fix is in letters.glyph_crop (Judge eval: 7 better, 0 worse); key letters are being re-read compute only, then this group re-runs (run10).

causes.title: Giant puzzles printed over two pages
causes.found: The 25x25 'Hard Clues' puzzles run their lists over two pages. Down 1-9 sit at the end of one page, and 'Hard Clues (con't.)' carries on from 10 on the next (1977-11 L040, looked at). Assembly links one page's block and misses the other; the start of a list is lost or shifted ('Rhododendron' read as D10, really D14), and a neighbouring feature's text can come along (1979-11 L072's 'Black ___' quiz).
causes.recommend: Hold. Tool fix in assembly: a heading 'Hard Clues (con't.)' continues the list from the facing page. And in clue numbering: two-line clues mustn't shift the numbers. Also needs the 'Easy Clues' second set (an accepted gap for now).

causes.title: Key found in run7; the text step's 'no key' is out of date
causes.found: These had no key when the text step ran; run7 found it on the page's other scan. Fixed in triage (request-key-settled): their key requests no longer count. What's left is real but small: Hot Stuff's key differs from the grid in 2 squares; Something Fishy has 7 doubted clues (cut-off quoted clues); Figure This's A36 lost its '2 wds.'; the 1977-11 illustrated crossword lost a clue's text and two drawings are cut off.
causes.recommend: Ready: good enough, with the doubts flagged on the proof page (as for Judge). Hot Stuff: check its 2 squares on the proof grid first.

causes.title: One or two key letters misread
causes.found: Single squares: 1978-09 L032 read I for T twice (67 Across, 55 Down); 1978-11 L032 R where S fits both words (A57/D54). The text step named the squares.
causes.recommend: Fix the squares on the proof page's grid (a minute each) then Ready.

causes.title: Variety puzzles, not standard crosswords
causes.found: RightAngles x2 (words bend at a right angle: no xd can hold them), Number Cross (digits in a grid), April Fools (a joke: every answer is 'nothing').
causes.recommend: Drop the two RightAngles. Number Cross and April Fools are your call: an xd can hold them, but neither is a crossword in gxd's sense.

causes.title: Warmup and Anglaise keys on the answer page, unmatched
causes.found: 1978-11's Answer Drawer page (leaf 76) has three 15x15 answer grids no puzzle took; the Anglaise and its warmup asked for their keys there.
causes.recommend: Trace in the watch (Assembled for 1978-11-01): probably keys whose black squares were read a few squares off. A matching fix, or a near-miss yes/no.

causes.title: A clue's text lost after a blank
causes.found: The same reading bug as the glance doubts: D40 and A98 lost the text after a blank or on the next line.
causes.recommend: Hold for the clue-reading fix above.

causes.title: A whole Down list missing
causes.found: Three Ways to Be: Across and key clean, no Down list linked at all.
causes.recommend: Open the boxes for 1978-01-01 in the watch: the Down list is probably outside every region box. A box fix restarts parts and assembly.

causes.title: Key a near miss
causes.found: Split-Quote (21x20): the harvest has a candidate key on leaf 108 that nearly matches (key-candidates.tsv).
causes.recommend: A yes/no on the candidate in the watch's questions.

causes.title: Title and byline read as one line
causes.found: 'Crossword à l'Anglaise by Doug and Janis Heller' was one OCR line. Fixed: the byline rule now takes names joined by 'and' (headers.py and proof.html), so the title and byline split.
